Éamon de Valera [ a ] (14 October 1882 – 29 August 1975) was an Irish statesman. He served as the president of Ireland from 1959 to 1973, and three terms as prime minister. [ b ] He had a leading role in introducing the Constitution of Ireland in 1937, [ 3 ] [ 4 ] and was a dominant figure in Irish political circles from the early 1930s to the late 1960s, when he served terms as both the head of government and head of state .
